old: "In Hungarian reported speech, the tense of the original statement is preserved (unlike English backshifting). The reporting clause regularly includes the demonstrative pronoun *azt*: *Azt mondta, hogy szívesen eljön.* ('He said he would gladly come' - original: 'Szívesen eljövök')."
new: "You know reported statements from B1 Unit 25. The tense of the original statement stays the same (unlike English backshifting), and only the person changes: *Szívesen eljövök* ('I will gladly come') becomes *Azt mondta, hogy szívesen eljön* ('He said he would gladly come'). The main clause usually has *azt* before *hogy*; you can also say *azt mesélte, hogy …* ('told that …')."
why: reported statements (reported-speech-statements, B1 Unit 25) were presented as new

old: "Key formulas include: *Szeretettel meghívjuk Önt/téged...*, *Nagy örömünkre szolgálna, ha eljönne...*, *Örömmel teszünk eleget a meghívásnak*, and *Hálásan köszönjük a vendégszeretetet.*"
new: "Key formulas for invitations: *Szeretettel meghívjuk Önt/téged …* ('We warmly invite you …'; *Ön* is the polite 'you' from A1 Unit 25), *Nagy örömünkre szolgálna, ha eljönne …* ('It would give us great pleasure if you came …': *ha* + conditional, A2 Unit 28), *Örömmel teszünk eleget a meghívásnak* ('We gladly accept the invitation': *eleget tesz* takes *-nak/-nek*) and *Hálásan köszönjük a vendégszeretetet.* ('We gratefully thank you for the hospitality.')."
why: formula list with no explanation; adds the recaps (Ön A1 Unit 25, ha + conditional A2 Unit 28) and the -nak/-nek of eleget tesz

old: "Indirect yes/no questions use the enclitic interrogative particle *-e* attached to the finite verb or predicate, or the polite interrogative particle *vajon*: *Azt kérdezte, hogy ráérsz-e ma este.* ('He asked whether you were free tonight'). In wh-questions, the question word follows *hogy*: *Azt kérdezte, hogy mikor kezdődik a megbeszélés.*"
new: "You know indirect questions from B1 Unit 25. A yes/no question uses *-e* on the word that carries the question: *Azt kérdezte, hogy ráérsz-e ma este.* ('He asked whether you were free tonight'). *Vajon* ('I wonder', A2 Unit 28) can be added when you wonder about the answer; the *-e* stays. In questions with a question word, that word follows *hogy*: *Azt kérdezte, hogy mikor kezdődik a megbeszélés.*"
why: indirect questions (B1 Unit 25) were presented as new, and *vajon* was called a 'polite interrogative particle' (it means 'I wonder')

old: "Constructive conflict resolution employs specific idioms: *félreértés tisztázása* ('clearing up a misunderstanding'), *dűlőre jut vkivel* ('reaching an accord/coming to terms'), *kompromisszumot köt* ('striking a compromise'), and *közös nevezőre jut* ('finding common ground')."
new: "Four phrases for settling a disagreement: *félreértés tisztázása* ('clearing up a misunderstanding'; *tisztázás* is a verbal noun in *-ás*, B1 Unit 31), *dűlőre jut vkivel* ('comes to terms with sb', with *-val/-vel*), *kompromisszumot köt* ('strikes a compromise', with the accusative *-t*) and *közös nevezőre jut* ('finds common ground', with *-ra/-re*)."
why: phrase list with no explanation; adds the recaps

old: "When reporting commands, advice, or requests, Hungarian uses the subjunctive mood (*-j-*) in the dependent clause: *Arra kért, hogy segítsek neki.* ('He asked me to help him'). *Megtiltotta, hogy továbbadjuk a titkot.* ('He forbade us to pass on the secret')."
new: "You know *hogy* + the *-jon/-jen* form from B1 Unit 5. New here: you use it to report a request or a command, and the person changes to fit the new speaker. *Arra kért, hogy segítsek neki.* ('He asked me to help him'; the request was *Segíts!*). *Megtiltotta, hogy továbbadjuk a titkot.* ('He forbade us to pass on the secret'). The main clause often has *arra* (with *kér*) or *azt* (with *mond*), and the verb after *hogy* is in the subjunctive (the *-j-* form)."
why: the screen presented the subjunctive as new without the B1 Unit 5 recap; says what is new (reporting a request or command)

old: "*Megbízik vkiben* (trusts in someone - inessive *-ban/-ben*), *a bizalmába fogad vkit* (takes someone into one's confidence - illative *-ba/-be*), *visszaél a bizalommal* (abuses trust - instrumental *-val/-vel*), *titkot tart* (keeps a secret)."
new: "*Megbízik vkiben* ('trusts in someone', with *-ban/-ben*; compare *bízik benne* from A2 Unit 33), *a bizalmába fogad vkit* ('takes someone into one's confidence', with *-ba/-be*), *visszaél a bizalommal* ('abuses trust', with *-val/-vel*) and *titkot tart* ('keeps a secret', with the accusative *-t*)."
why: phrase list; adds the bízik benne recap (A2 Unit 33) and names the endings in plain terms

old: "The reciprocal pronoun *egymás* ('each other / one another') declines with all Hungarian case suffixes: *egymást* (accusative), *egymásnak* (dative), *egymással* (instrumental), *egymásért* (causal-final), *egymás mellett* (postpositional). It expresses mutual solidarity and community bond."
new: "You know *egymás* ('each other') from A2 Unit 5 and B1 Unit 9. It takes the case endings like a noun: *egymást* (accusative), *egymásnak* (dative), *egymással* ('with each other'), *egymásért* ('for each other'; verbs governing *-ért*, A2 Unit 8) and *egymás mellett* ('next to each other'). *Kölcsönösen* ('mutually') stresses that both sides do it."
why: *egymás* (A2 Unit 5, B1 Unit 9) was presented as new

new: "*Összetart a csapat* ('the team sticks together'), *hű marad az elveihez/barátaihoz* ('remains faithful to his principles/friends': you know *hű marad … -hoz/-hez/-höz* from B1 Unit 51) and *bajtársiasságot tanúsít* ('shows camaraderie')."

old: "Concessive relations contrast an unexpected outcome with an obstacle: *bár* ('although'), *noha* ('even though'), *annak ellenére, hogy...* ('in spite of the fact that...'). The main clause often opens with *mégis* ('yet / nevertheless'): *Bár fáradt volt, mégis elment a találkozóra.*"

The main clause often opens with *mégis* ('nevertheless'): *Bár fáradt volt, mégis elment a találkozóra.*"
